articles.title: ESPHome stops its web interface exposing password-field contents
articles.dek: Web interface versions 2 and 3 stop sending the secret behind a masked field; deprecated version 1 remains affected.
body: ESPHome removes the contents of password-mode text fields from its web server’s data responses. The interface displayed a mask, but another field in the same response still carried the real value, exposing the secret to anyone able to read that response.

J. Nick Koston corrects both the live event stream and the individual data endpoint used by web interface versions 2 and 3. Password inputs start empty and still accept a replacement value. Deprecated version 1 renders the raw value in its own page and is not covered by this correction.

pullRequests.title: [web_server] Mask the value of a password text entity, not only its state

articles.title: ESPHome installs firmware on Pico and nRF52 boards through the browser
articles.dek: Device Builder extends USB installation to Raspberry Pi Pico and compatible Nordic boards, with browser-based Pico logs too.
body: ESPHome Device Builder adds browser-based USB installation for Raspberry Pi Pico boards and for nRF52 devices that use the Adafruit bootloader. Makers can compile a configuration and install its firmware from the dashboard. The nRF52 installer also joins the standalone ESPHome Web tool.

The Pico installer supports RP2040 boards, including a tested Pico W, and refuses RP2350 images. A Pico already running ESPHome can restart into its installation mode automatically; a first installation needs that mode selected by hand. Browsers without WebUSB download the firmware with instructions to copy it to the Pico instead. Pico owners also gain USB logs in the browser.

Contributor tomaszduda23 makes a first contribution to the Device Builder frontend with the nRF52 installer, drawing on jonasniesner’s tools. J. Nick Koston adds the Pico installer and logs. A companion nRF52 correction gives the bootloader enough time to erase memory without the device restarting during installation.

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps history visible after a database interruption
articles.dek: A recovered connection no longer leaves unchanged devices with blank history until a restart.
body: Home Assistant preserves the start of a history graph after a temporary database interruption. Previously, recovery could make devices with no changes during the selected period appear as empty rows, even though their recorded data was intact.

Kailash Nelson keeps the information needed to show each device’s state at the beginning of the requested period. The correction avoids the restart previously needed to restore that view. J. Nick Koston reviewed the work.

pullRequests.title: Preserve recorder oldest timestamp across session recovery

articles.title: Nabu Casa explains how remote access chooses a server
articles.dek: New guidance covers latency measurements, blocked pings and connection trouble after a server change.
body: A new Nabu Casa guide explains why the closest Home Assistant Cloud server may not provide the quickest remote connection. According to the guide, selection uses measured round-trip times alongside available server capacity, with a preference for keeping the existing server to avoid needless moves.

The guide says blocked pings do not prevent remote access: if no measurement target answers, the previous selection method remains in use. After a server change, a stale DNS record can temporarily prevent access; clearing that cache can restore the connection. It also explains how to find latency results in debug logs and what measurement information goes back to Nabu Casa.

articles.title: Home Assistant sets the charging current for Silla Prism
articles.dek: A new control adjusts the charger’s user setting from 6 to 32 amps.
body: Silla Prism owners gain a Home Assistant control for their charger’s maximum charging current. It reads the current user setting and adjusts it in one-amp steps from 6 to 32 amps, matching the charger’s own plus and minus controls.
Ermanno Baschiera adds the setting alongside the Solar, Normal and Pause modes reported on September 11. This does not expose the charger’s separate external load-balancing limit.

articles.title: Matter.js rejects pairing requests that can stall a controller
articles.dek: Controllers check the device’s requested cryptographic workload before starting it.
body: Controllers built with Matter.js stop accepting an unrestricted amount of cryptographic work requested by a device during pairing. An excessive value could occupy a worker thread for minutes and delay other encryption and file operations sharing the same pool.

Ingo Fischer checks that request against the protocol’s permitted range before starting the calculation. An invalid response ends the attempt at that address while allowing other addresses to be tried.

pullRequests.title: fix(protocol): bound PBKDF iterations in PBKDFParamResponse

articles.title: Home Assistant refreshes Tuya’s login code when it is needed
articles.dek: Reconnecting an expired account no longer presents a QR code that expired while the prompt waited.
body: Home Assistant fetches a fresh Tuya QR code when someone confirms they want to reconnect the account. Previously, it requested the code as soon as authentication expired and kept it while waiting, so opening the prompt later could present an unusable code that only a restart replaced.
The correction applies to reconnecting an existing account. Initial setup already creates a new code.

articles.title: Assist adds Basque commands for light colours and warmth
articles.dek: Lighting commands cover named lights, rooms and floors, with floor-wide brightness control too.
body: Basque speakers gain Assist commands for changing light colours and colour temperature, whether addressing a named light, a room or a floor. They can also set brightness across a floor.

Urtzi Odriozola adds Basque colour names and their grammatical forms, alongside the responses to these requests. The work extends the on-and-off commands reported on September 23 with control over how the lights look.
